DCI.text: Distributor of IT hardware, networking and cybersecurity products. Demand is strong: ==products revenue +40%== and ==security software +29%== in Q2. Oct–Dec is the ==festive and year-end IT buying season==, which usually lifts distributor volumes. Watch: the business needs more working capital (borrowings up to ₹123 cr, inventory up), so higher interest cost can eat into profit.

MODIS.text: Real-estate redevelopment developer. ==Bookings ₹202 cr in H1 vs ₹54 cr== a year ago, at ==8% higher average price== per sq ft. ==₹156 cr of sold flats is still to be booked as revenue==, and two projects are near completion (==Rashmi Square 80% built==, Rashmi Signature 62%), so revenue recognition should rise. A new redevelopment project was added, and ₹505 cr of unsold flats is future potential. Watch: two big projects (Icon, Avenue) are still early-stage.

PANACHE.text: Supplies IT hardware, including laptops. ==New ₹51.4 cr laptop order== from an IT-sector customer (2 Nov 2026), to be delivered ==within about 30 days==: more than 60% of last quarter's sales, falling fully in Oct–Dec. Repeat large orders from corporate and IT customers are driving demand. Watch: orders are lumpy and the customer is not named.

526433.text: Engineering and product R&D services company with design centres in India and abroad (USA, UK, Singapore, Japan, Mexico). Demand from overseas clients is scaling fast: ==quarterly sales jumped from ₹199 cr to ₹268 cr in one quarter==. Next quarter is compared with a ==weak Dec 2025 quarter==, so high growth is likely. No specific order or capacity news found. Watch: promoter holding fell from 57.4% to 53.5% in October.

530477.text: Makes pharma excipients (co-polymers used in tablet coatings and formulations) for domestic and export pharma companies: steady, repeat demand. Sales have risen for 3 quarters in a row, to a ==record ₹44 cr==. No new capacity or big orders announced, so growth depends on pharma volumes and export demand continuing. Margins stay high because raw-material costs have been stable.

544406.text: IT-infrastructure, cybersecurity and managed-services provider. ==Added 10+ large enterprise clients== (Sun Pharma, Jio 5G, IDBI Bank, Kotak Bank, IDFC First Bank and others) and won a ==₹27 cr cybersecurity order==. Banks bring 56% of revenue, and Oct–Dec is usually a ==strong quarter for bank IT spending==. It is expanding into managed services and public-sector deals. Watch: dependence on bank budgets.

ARIES.text: Specialty plant-nutrient maker (chelated micronutrients, 134 brands); it pioneered chelation technology in India. Oct–Dec covers ==rabi sowing==, a key season for micronutrient demand. The Sep-quarter results on ==13 Nov 2026== will show how kharif demand and margins went, the best clue for the next quarter. Watch: weather, raw-material (fertiliser input) prices and delays in subsidy payments.

AVTNPL.text: Makes plant-based extracts and natural ingredients (A.V. Thomas Group) for food, beverage, animal-nutrition and nutraceutical customers, largely exported. ==Five quarters of rising sales== show strong demand for natural ingredients. The Sep-quarter results on ==11 Nov 2026== will confirm the trend. Watch: crop and raw-material prices, currency moves and dependence on a few export customers.

ESCONET.text: IT-infrastructure, high-performance computing (HPC) and AI-server integrator with its own ==HexaData server brand== (Red Hat certified), partnering Nvidia, Dell, AMD and Intel. Demand is coming from ==AI & HPC computing== and government digitisation: a ==₹25.7 cr C-DAC Pune hardware order== (Jul 2026), after a ₹20 cr, 340-server order from Info Edge. Its ==Singapore subsidiary is now about 31% of revenue==, a new market. ZeaCloud subsidiary is applying for ==MeitY empanelment as a sovereign government cloud== in H2 FY27; management sees a 2–3 year growth runway. Watch: thin margins on hardware resale.

GANDHAR.text: Specialty oils maker (white oils, petroleum jelly, transformer oils, lubricants) for personal-care, pharma, power and auto customers. Profit jumped on a ==much wider margin spread (₹388 vs ₹130 per kl)== and ==record revenue (+73%)==, with robust demand across industrial segments; CRISIL reaffirmed A+ and raised bank limits. Watch: margins depend on crude/base-oil spreads, which can reverse; receivables nearly doubled to ₹1,339 cr; one-time flood loss at the Silvassa unit.

TATVA.text: Specialty chemicals maker: phase-transfer catalysts, ==structure-directing agents (SDAs) for Euro 7 emission catalysts==, battery electrolyte salts, agro and pharma intermediates. Q2 was its ==highest-ever quarter==. Drivers: SDA demand from Euro 7 norms, ==electrolyte salts moving to commercial scale==, new agrochemical products and a first pharma product; ==5 semiconductor chemicals in customer qualification==. Watch: solvent prices (+60–100%) and freight (+100%) hurt Q2; management expects both to normalise in Q3.

PRIZOR.text: Gujarat-based CCTV and AI-camera brand (Prizor Plus: face recognition, number-plate reading, speed detection), plus smart TVs and classroom touch panels, sold through 9,000+ dealers. Catalyst: ==BIS-ER certification (Jan 2026)== opens government orders, and the ==April 2026 ban on non-compliant IP cameras== could shift ₹6,000–8,000 cr of yearly demand to certified makers. ==Plant runs at only 15–20% of its 50 lakh-unit capacity==, so growth needs little new investment; new Kolkata branch; raised ₹119 cr. Watch: competition from large CCTV brands.

BHAGERIA.text: Dyes and dye-intermediates maker (plus a solar power business). Q2 revenue more than doubled to ₹450 cr and EBITDA margin rose to 18% on ==higher realisations in key chemical products== and better cost absorption at higher volumes. Watch: dye-intermediate prices are cyclical; raw-material costs and export demand (trade policy, currency) can swing margins quickly.

WSTCSTPAPR.text: Paper and paperboard maker that also makes ==optical fibre and fibre-optic cables==. The board approved a ==₹290 cr optical-fibre expansion== (4.0 mn fkm of fibre and 3.1 mn fkm of cable a year, ready by Q3 FY29), nearly doubling that business on telecom and data-centre fibre demand. Watch: paper prices, wood and pulp costs, and cheap paper imports.

NITINSPIN.text: Cotton yarn and fabric maker; ==68% of sales are exports==. Q2 margins jumped on ==higher yarn prices== and full capacity use, with ==record fabric revenue== (woven sales 11.8 mn m vs 8.3 mn). Catalyst: a new ==35 mn metre/year greige fabric plant is starting up== (trial output already), so more of its own yarn becomes higher-value fabric; management cites ==favourable trade policies==. Watch: borrowings doubled to ₹1,183 cr for the expansion; cotton prices.

DPABHUSHAN.text: Gold and diamond jewellery retailer with 14 showrooms in Central India. ==Navratri moved from September (last year) to October this year==, so festive and wedding sales shift into Oct–Dec: management expects Q3 FY27 to be its ==highest-ever quarter==. ==3 new showrooms== in FY27 (Dhar, Dahod, Jabalpur, opened 30 Oct), 3–4 more by March 2027, plus a new e-commerce app. Watch: sharp gold-price swings can slow buying.

504240.text: Cables and wires maker that also does ==power EPC== and railway and telecom work. Order book ==₹471.5 cr (1.4× quarterly revenue)==, 87% of it higher-margin EPC; EPC revenue +68% and telecom +100% in H1. Catalyst: executing this EPC order book over the coming quarters. Watch: copper and aluminium prices (material cost +71%); no project timelines disclosed.

VRLLOG.text: India's largest part-load (LTL) road transporter. ==Freight rates raised about 9% this year== (April and May), lifting EBITDA margin to 23%; ==67 new branches in H1==, expanding into UP, Bihar and West Bengal. Management targets ==9–10% tonnage growth== in H2. Debt is falling and a buyback is coming. Watch: diesel and toll costs; a big diesel price cut could force rate cuts.

STOVEKRAFT.text: Kitchen appliances and cookware maker (Pigeon, Gilma). Catalysts: ==Pigeon value range and retail expansion==, ==Gilma relaunched as a premium brand==, strong e-commerce and general-trade growth, a growing own exclusive-store network, and ==festive demand in Oct–Dec==; integrated manufacturing supports margins. Watch: metal and raw-material inflation, and competition.

WHEELS.text: Steel and alloy wheel maker for trucks, tractors, cars and construction equipment, plus industrial components (wind, hydraulics). Automotive profit ==+70%== on strong demand; ==₹400–450 cr capex in FY27== for steel wheels, ==cast alloy wheels==, construction and mining wheels, air suspension and large machining. Watch: industrial-segment profit fell 34%; free cash flow is negative during the capex; steel prices.

SAHASRA.text: Electronics maker (memory modules, microSD cards, LED and EMS work) that is moving into ==semiconductor packaging==: about ₹350 cr planned over three years for one of India's first chip-packaging units. It has begun ==exporting Made-in-India microSD cards== (partnership with Germany's HAMA). Growth comes from India's electronics and chip localisation push. Watch: big capex for its size; Sep-quarter results not yet on Screener.

RAPIDFLEET.text: Transport and fleet-deployment services company. Has ==₹230 cr of FY27 orders across five sectors==, including ==₹53 cr from renewable-energy logistics== (wind/solar equipment moving), a new and growing line. Added 25 vehicles (₹12.35 cr capex), taking the fleet ==above 300==; Q1 FY27 revenue +63%. Watch: Sep-quarter results not yet on Screener; customer concentration and diesel costs.

SHREEPUSHK.text: Dye-intermediates, chemicals and fertiliser (SSP, soil conditioner) maker. Chemical sales ==+86% to ₹245 cr== despite lower volume, meaning ==much higher value per tonne== (better prices or product mix); fertiliser sales +27% with volume +9%. New ==₹70 cr Ratnagiri plant== approved (commissioning by March 2028), part of a 69,000 TPA capacity roadmap, partly funded by warrants. Watch: receivables jumped to ₹332 cr and H1 operating cash flow was negative.

THEJO.text: Wear-protection, conveyor and bulk-material-handling solutions for mining, cement, steel and ports, with subsidiaries in ==Australia and Brazil==. Growth comes from ==mining, cement and steel capex cycles== and execution of its order backlog; won a ==Vale Brazil order== (July 2026). Q1 FY27 revenue +32%, margin 14.2%. Watch: rubber and steel prices; overseas project delays; Sep-quarter results not yet on Screener.

CEIGALL.text: Road, highway and specialised EPC contractor (elevated roads, bridges, tunnels). ==Order book about ₹18,500 cr== (roughly 5× yearly revenue); new wins include a ==₹981 cr NHAI project== and a ₹705 cr border road in Arunachal; FY27 order-inflow target ₹6,000 cr. Management ==raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 15%+==. Watch: margin guidance is conservative (11–12.5%) because of the monsoon; working capital in HAM projects.

AYMSYNTEX.text: Synthetic yarn maker (polyester and nylon filament, carpet and industrial yarns) for textiles, floor coverings and automotive fabrics. Q2 revenue ==+29% to ₹450 cr== on ==higher capacity utilisation== and steady demand for specialty filament yarns. Watch: polymer (PTA/MEG, nylon chips) price swings must be passed on to protect margins; export demand and currency.

YASHO.text: Specialty chemicals maker (rubber chemicals, lubricant additives, aroma chemicals), with a large new plant ramping up. ==Exports more than doubled==; volumes +42% in Q1 with utilisation above 65%. Catalyst: a ==15-year lubricant-additive supply deal with an MNC== (trial production Q4 FY27, commercial Q1 FY28). Management ==raised FY27 capex to ₹250 cr== and its ==FY28 revenue target to above ₹1,600 cr==. Watch: new borrowings for capex; Kacholia-backed stock can be volatile.

SHUKRAPHAR.text: Renamed ==Shukra Medtech==: pharma formulations, medical technology and analytical testing. Revenue jumped about 7× (₹44 cr in Q2) because ==export customers now drive most of the growth==; the ==MedTech arm (₹12.5 cr in Q2)== is management's top priority and will take a few quarters to scale. Watch: management itself says exports are new and must become repeatable; higher inventory and receivables.

NRAIL.text: Duplex board and paper maker (packaging board for FMCG, pharma and industrial cartons). ==Duplex-board capacity raised from 725 to 900 tonnes a day== (total about 5 lakh tonnes a year); the new lines are ramping up. Q2 revenue ==+28% to ₹670 cr== on volume growth and steady packaging demand; ICRA reaffirmed its ratings. Watch: waste-paper and imported-pulp prices, energy costs and regional competition.

ANTELOPUS.text: Oil and gas producer (Cambay basin, KG onshore). Production about ==2,000 barrels/day in October== (FY26 exit 1,758); targets ==2,500 by end-FY27, 3,500 by FY28 and 5,000 by FY29==. Seven new Karjisan wells this year (one starting soon), Bakrol fracking campaign complete, and ==seven newly acquired KG discoveries== to develop. Debt-free, about 71% EBITDA margin. Watch: crude prices, well results and KG costs (about $10 mn a well).

XPROINDIA.text: Maker of dielectric (capacitor) BOPP films and packaging films; ==meets about a third of Indian demand==, the rest is imported. ==New Barjora line (March 2026) doubled film capacity to about 8,000 tonnes a year== and is ramping up; a ==second line in the UAE starts this year==. Demand from capacitors for power grids, renewables, data centres and EV electronics; import substitution and exports to the US and Europe. Watch: debt of about ₹289 cr and ramp-up speed.

LRRPL.text: Rubber recycler turning scrap tyres into reclaimed rubber and crumb for tyre and rubber-goods makers. ==H1 FY27 revenue +65% to ₹36 cr, PAT +223% to ₹3.2 cr==, with EBITDA margin near ==16%==. Growth is driven by more tyre-maker demand for recycled rubber (green-content push) and fuller use of the new capacity; management plans further capacity-led growth. Watch: small size, scrap-tyre price swings, and customer concentration in tyre companies.

ASIANENE.text: Oilfield and mineral services company. ==Order book about ₹1,633 cr== (oil & gas 59%, mining 41%), including ==its first order outside Coal India (GSECL Ukai)==. ==H1 revenue +148% to ₹538 cr, PAT ₹29.8 cr==. Management targets ==about ₹3,000 cr revenue and ₹700 cr EBITDA by FY29/30==. More coal-handling and mine-development contracts give multi-year work. Watch: business is weighted to H2, and Kuiper operations were disrupted.

OBSCP.text: Forging and stamping maker moving from auto into exports, marine and defence. ==Exports +173% to ₹49 cr==; ==non-auto revenue more than doubled==. ==Order book above ₹1,200 cr== (55% exports, 5–6 year life). Got ==AS9100D aerospace certification== and an ==₹8.9 cr Elbit fuze order==. Spare forging capacity and new land support further growth. Watch: working capital rose 69%.

AEROFLEX.text: Stainless-steel flexible hose and assemblies maker. ==Q2 income +87% to ₹208 cr, PAT +157% to ₹36.6 cr==. ==SS hose capacity raised to 20 mn metres a year== and ==liquid-cooling skid assemblies to 12,000 a year==, aimed at ==AI data-centre cooling demand==. Management targets about 35% growth in FY27. Merging the Hyd-Air subsidiary simplifies the group. Watch: nickel/steel price swings and export demand.

KRISHNADEF.text: Defence and naval materials maker. ==Q2 revenue +56% to ₹75 cr== with a ==record 26.9% EBITDA margin==. ==Order book ₹109 cr; tender pipeline ₹305 cr==. New products: ammunition components (MoU), ==barrier exports to Belgium==, underwater welding consumables (iDEX), and the ==JAYA autonomous underwater vehicle== with Navy ISR/ASW development contracts; a Chennai AUV test facility is coming. Watch: lumpy defence orders and small order book vs pipeline.

544501.text: Power transmission & distribution EPC (substations, smart grid) plus solar. ==Order book ₹1,067 cr==, about ==3.5× FY26 revenue==. ==Seven Q2 orders worth ₹395 cr, all outside Bihar== – Bihar's share fell to ==55% from 82%==. ==H1 revenue +73% to ₹213 cr; Q2 PAT +108%==. A 3-year Odisha maintenance contract (~₹60 cr a year) started 1 Oct; tender pipeline ~₹19,150 cr. Watch: debt rising to ~₹240 cr, cash burn while growing, revenue weighted to H2.

SHAILY.text: Precision plastic parts maker; healthcare (drug-delivery pens) is now the main engine. ==Q2 standalone revenue +31% to ₹310 cr, PAT +63% to ₹67 cr==. In Q1, ==healthcare revenue rose 85% and became 51% of sales==, driven by ==GLP-1 (weight-loss) injector pen components==; pen capacity was being ==doubled from 40 mn to 80 mn units==. Industrial +25%. Watch: consumer business weak (Europe/US), oral GLP-1 tablets, client approval delays.

TAMBOLIIN.text: Investment-casting maker for pumps, valves, pneumatics, auto and aerospace, exporting to 27+ countries. ==Q2 income +20%, PAT +76% to ₹3.4 cr==, ==EBITDA margin up to 25% from 20%==. ==Fortune-100 OEM programme: 50+ parts, potential ₹20 cr+ yearly revenue== over 2–3 years; first development orders received. Adding CNC machining capacity, full use expected by FY28. Watch: OEM approvals timing and Europe demand.

MACPOWER.text: CNC machine-tool maker. ==Q2 revenue +40% to ₹120 cr, PAT +44%==. ==Demand exceeds supply== – it refunds 10–20 machine orders a month due to delivery delays; expects ==2,300–2,400 machines this year==. High-margin ==NEXA range is ~40% of orders== (target 50%). ==New 13-acre plant (+2,500 machines) from about Q2 FY28==; price hikes planned after Q3. Defence orders being executed. Watch: big capacity jump only from FY29, plant timing.

KANPRPLA.text: FIBC (jumbo bag) and woven packaging exporter. ==Q2 revenue +42% to ₹235 cr, PAT more than doubled (+114%)==. New growth legs: ==non-woven fabric line (from Nov 2026, ₹100–120 cr revenue over FY27–28)==, ==yarn capacity 7,000→10,000 t==, and ==FIBC capacity rising to 24,000 t==; Essegomma JV adds ₹10–12 cr next year. FIBC volume growth guided 5–10% this year, ~20% next. Watch: high polymer prices, freight costs, flat order book.

TEAMTECH.text: Maker and renter of construction formwork (aluminium/steel shuttering) for builders and infra contractors; listed on NSE Emerge in May 2026. ==Targets ₹140 cr revenue by FY28 on capacity expansion== funded by the IPO. Won a ==₹9.44 cr Lloyds formwork order== (more than 10% of last year's revenue), executed within 90 days. Demand comes from housing and infra building. Watch: small size, lumpy orders, and reported numbers need checking against filings.

543619.text: Railway electronics maker (Concord Control). ==Order book about ₹846 cr – nearly 4× FY26 revenue==, to be executed in 18–24 months; ==₹308 cr of new orders in H1==, including a ==₹280 cr Kavach 4.0 train-safety order== from Indian Railways. ==H1 FY27 revenue +95% to ₹159 cr, PAT +95% to ₹31 cr==. Its tech runs on 8,000+ locomotives. New leg: Fusion Electronics (flex PCBs) could reach ~₹400 cr after doubling capacity. Watch: very long cash cycle (338 days), Kavach still scaling.

543787.text: Macfos runs Robu.in, an online store for robotics, drone, IoT and electronics parts (1 lakh+ items). ==Q2 revenue +44% to ₹99 cr, PAT +45% to ₹7.4 cr==. Customers grew to ==67,480 from 59,771== with good repeat buying, and ==corporate/defence customers are rising==. Own brands (ROBU 2.0) are adding hundreds of new items, especially ==drone parts==, which earn better margins. Watch: margins slipped in Q1, higher costs and slow-moving stock.

524717.text: Maker of microbiology culture media, peptones and lab reagents used by pharma, vaccine and food-testing labs. ==Q2 revenue +41% to ₹76 cr==, the highest in five quarters, and ==PAT +62% to ₹12.6 cr==. ==Net margin rose to 16.4% from 14.3%==, so profit is growing faster than sales. Growing demand from pharma quality testing and biotech fermentation supports volumes. Watch: quarterly sales swing a lot (₹49–76 cr), so the higher margin must hold.

543920.text: Makes submarine and warship fluid systems for the Navy. ==Won a ₹27.85 cr Mazagon Dock submarine equipment order== (delivery by Aug 2027) plus several Navy spares orders; total order book reported above ₹600 cr. On 6 Nov 2026 it ==approved a joint venture with TKMS Atlas Elektronik (Germany)==, linked to the Navy's new submarine programmes. FY26 sales +43%, ~28% operating margin. Watch: negative cash flow, debtor days ~183.
sources: HDFC Sky – CFF ₹27.85 cr Mazagon Dock order

513472.text: Heavy castings and fabrication for steel and power plants (SAIL fabrication partner; SMS, Hindustan Zinc, Thyssenkrupp, BHEL). ==Order book crossed ₹130 cr== with 4–6 month execution. ==RDSO approval to test cast-steel bogies, side frames and bolsters== lets it re-enter railway wagon parts – ==about ₹50 cr railway revenue expected in FY27==; management eyes ==₹300 cr revenue in FY27== (FY26 ₹203 cr). Watch: railway approval timing and steel-sector capex cycles.
sources: PSU Connect – Simplex order book ₹130 cr

515008.text: India's leading exporter of extra-high-voltage porcelain insulators for power transmission lines. ==Q1 FY27 profit +80% to ₹29 cr== after FY26 profit doubled; Q4 EBITDA margin jumped to ==15.7% from 11.2%==. Demand comes from ==grid expansion, renewable-energy transmission and railway electrification==; exports are 30%+ of insulator sales. Debt-free. Watch: natural-gas and raw-material costs, pending merger with Terry Towels (auditor queries).

539984.text: High-tension porcelain insulator maker for power transmission. ==Q2 revenue +148% to ₹171 cr== and ==profit ₹55 cr vs a ₹43 cr loss== a year ago, driven by ==strong growth in high-tension insulators==. Revenue grew far faster than costs, so margins expanded sharply. Grid and renewable transmission spending keeps demand high. Watch: ₹155 cr related-party loan, and whether this turnaround lasts.

542669.text: Steel processing: galvanising, rolling mill, pipes & tubes, logistics. ==Q2 revenue +25% to ₹182 cr==; ==rolling mill sales +214% and pipes +93%== as utilisation rose. The ==Bokaro colour-coated steel line got approval to start (5 Oct 2026)== – a new higher-value product. ₹516 cr spent on Bokaro expansion. Watch: Q2 profit growth (+43%) came mostly from other income; operating margin fell to 19% and net debt rose to ₹589 cr.
sources: The Week – BMW Industries Q2 FY27

543542.text: Nagpur real-estate developer (Kesar Lands brand). ==Pipeline of 29 projects with gross value above ₹5,100 cr== (12.2 mn sq ft) giving ==3–5 years of visibility==; another ==₹4,000 cr+ under evaluation==. Ranked 6th in India for revenue growth in Hurun Real Estate 150; FY26 revenue +64%. Moving to a long-term land bank to reduce land-price risk. Watch: revenue is lumpy, ₹2,000 cr+ investment needed, and the figures are management estimates.

BALUFORGE.text: Precision forging and machined parts maker, now moving strongly into defence. Won its ==first 155mm ERFB artillery shell order (10,000 units)== in Aug 2026, after a ==30,000-unit 152mm shell order== in June. The automated, robot-based Belgaum plant makes "ready-to-fill" shells. ==Q1 FY27 revenue +29% to ₹301 cr, PAT +16% to ₹66 cr==, EBITDA margin about 28%. Raising up to US$60 mn via FCCBs to fund growth. Watch: profit growing slower than sales, metal-price-linked pricing, 140 working-capital days.
sources: Construction World – Balu Forge Q1 FY27

DANISH.text: Transformer maker (inverter-duty and power transformers for solar and grid). ==H1 FY27 revenue +38% to ₹292 cr, PAT ₹38 cr==, EBITDA margin about 19%. ==Order book above ₹600 cr== for the next 6–9 months; management guides ==FY27 revenue above ₹700 cr== and aims to double exports to ~20%. Planning ==₹200 cr capex to raise capacity from 15,000 to 26,000 MVA==, adding ==400 kV transformers==. Watch: capex funded partly by debt, copper/CRGO steel prices.
sources: Arthneeti – Danish Power H1 FY27 presentation

DIFFNKG.text: Wear-resistance welding consumables, wear plates and heavy-engineering repair for cement, steel and power plants. ==Q2 revenue +51% to ₹126 cr, PAT +26%==. ==Order book ₹227 cr, up 30%== since March (heavy engineering ₹178 cr). New legs: ==roller orders from JSW and JSPL==, first vertical roller mill order, ==qualified for railway loco shells==, Abu Dhabi plant starting, Africa cement wins. Management guides 20–25% yearly growth. Watch: tungsten/alloy costs cut gross margin to 30%; margin recovery expected from Q4.

GALAPREC.text: Disc springs and precision fastening parts for wind, industrial and other machinery. ==Q2 revenue +31% to ₹94 cr, PAT +26%, operating profit +42%==. ==Order bookings up about 40%==; firm order book ~₹110 cr. ==New Chennai hot-dip galvanising plant== has started and opens new customers; ==first bulk order from an electrolyser (green hydrogen) maker==. Guidance: FY27 revenue growth 20–25%, EBITDA margin 17–19%. Land MoU at Wada for future capacity. Watch: margins still below guidance, lower currency hedging.
sources: Multibagg – Gala Q1 FY27 order growth

FCL.text: Specialty chemicals for textiles, cleaning, water treatment and oil & gas. ==Q1 FY27 revenue more than doubled (+164%) to ₹387 cr, PAT +93% to ₹48 cr==, mainly from the ==CrudeChem (US oilfield chemicals) acquisition==. ==Texas plant expansion commissioned==, taking total capacity to ==about 1.48 lakh tonnes a year==. Looking at more acquisitions abroad. Watch: growth is mostly acquisition-led; check that CrudeChem gains continue and new capacity gets used.

EIMCOELECO.text: Underground mining and construction equipment maker (loaders, drill machines). ==Q2 revenue +71% to ₹57 cr, PAT +47%, EBITDA doubled (+109%)== with margin 18.8%. ==Order book ₹133 cr vs ₹44 cr a year ago – three times higher==, giving strong visibility for coming quarters. More underground coal and metal mining by PSUs drives demand. Watch: CFO resigned in Q2; quarterly sales are lumpy.
sources: Free Press Journal – Eimco Elecon Q2 FY27

ACCENTMIC.text: Maker of microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) and other cellulose excipients – the filler used in pharma tablets, food and cosmetics; large export share. ==Q2 revenue +26% to ₹175 cr, PAT +72% to ₹31 cr==, operating profit +71%, so ==margins expanded sharply==. Company is ==almost debt-free== after cutting debt, and expanded capacity is filling up with pharma and export demand. Watch: promoter holding fell 1.6% last quarter; pulp price swings.

FAZE3Q.text: Home textiles exporter (rugs, bath mats, cushions, outdoor fabrics) mainly to US/EU retailers. ==Q2 income +29% to ₹268 cr – best September quarter ever==; ==PAT ₹15.5 cr vs a loss== last year. EBITDA margin up to ==13.3%== from customer price hikes, better dollar rate and operating leverage. ==PLI incentive approval (Jul 2026)== adds benefits from FY28; new product capacity by Q1 FY28. Management expects 20%+ growth in FY27. Watch: high cotton/polyester and freight costs, US tariff risk.

ASHIANA.text: Housing developer (senior living, kid-centric homes) in NCR, Rajasthan, Pune, Chennai. ==Q2 bookings ₹834 cr – about 2.75× last year's ₹303 cr==; ==H1 bookings ₹1,192 cr = 54% of the ₹2,200 cr FY27 target==. Bought ==28.5 acres in Pune (₹1,800 cr revenue potential)== and plans ₹1,000 cr more land buys in FY27, funded from its own cash. Handovers started at Gurugram projects, which will lift reported revenue. Watch: reported revenue lags bookings; approval delays.

PTCIL.text: Precision castings maker moving into titanium and superalloys for aerospace and defence. Subsidiary ==Aerolloy signed an Airbus agreement for titanium castings (A320neo, A330neo, A350)==. New defence orders: ==BrahMos missile sub-system==, a titanium part for the 105mm light tank (DRDO), and artillery gun parts. ==Q1 FY27 income +83% to ₹197 cr, PAT +466% to ₹29 cr==; EBITDA margin up to ==27.5%==. Lucknow titanium mill being built. Watch: Airbus/defence qualification takes time; no order-book figure given.

GOLDIAM.text: Lab-grown diamond jewellery exporter to large US retailers. ==Q2 income +44% to ₹292 cr, PAT +58% to ₹49 cr==, EBITDA margin ~25%. ==Lab-grown is 91% of export sales==. ==Export order book about ₹225 cr==, to be executed in 3–4 months. Own retail brand ==ORIGEM now has 29 stores== (₹11 cr quarterly sales) – a new growth leg in India. Watch: heavy dependence on US retailers (58% of stock on consignment) and lab-grown price falls.

INDIAGLYCO.text: Chemicals, potable spirits, ethanol and nutraceuticals company. ==Q1 FY27 PAT +32% to ₹97 cr==, helped by ==lower interest (finance cost ₹25 cr vs ₹45 cr)==. ==Demerger into 3 listed companies approved by NCLT== (chemicals, IGL Spirits, Ennature Biopharma). Guidance: ==Spirits EBITDA above ₹500 cr in FY27==, chemicals ₹200 cr+, Ennature ₹50 cr+. Ennature had its best quarter (+65%) with nicotine expansion. Watch: propylene oxide supply hurting chemical margins; demerger date pending.
sources: Multibagg – India Glycols Q1 FY27 demerger

MANINDS.text: Large-diameter line pipe maker for oil, gas and water projects. ==Q1 FY27 PAT more than doubled (+118%) to ₹61 cr==, ==record EBITDA margin 14.6%==. ==Order book ~₹3,600 cr== and ==bid pipeline ~₹24,000 cr== (70% Middle East). Bought ==Saudi pipe maker NPC== – full contribution from Q2. ==Jammu stainless seamless pipe plant (₹200–300 cr first-year sales) and Dammam coating plant due March 2027==. FY27 revenue guided ~₹5,000 cr. Watch: debt peaking near ₹1,600 cr, project delays.
sources: Indian Chemical News – MAN record Q1

KMEW.text: Port dredging, marine services and shipbuilding company. ==H1 FY27 revenue +89% to ₹186 cr, PAT +267% to ₹84 cr== (45% margin). Won a ==₹279 cr third green tug contract from Mumbai Port==; order book about ₹1,100–1,400 cr. Building its own ==Palghar shipyard== (green tugs, dredgers, electric ferries). ==Growth guidance raised from 35% to 60%==; target ₹1,000 cr revenue by FY29. Watch: cash flow well below profit, borrowings ₹272 cr, shipyard execution.

SEAMECLTD.text: Offshore diving-support and multi-purpose vessel operator, mainly for ONGC oilfield work. ==Q2 revenue doubled (+103%) to ₹198 cr==, ==PAT ₹50.5 cr vs a ₹26 cr loss== last year, EBITDA margin up to ==19.3% from 8%==. Demand backdrop: ==ONGC capex ~₹32,000 cr in FY27== and the Samudra Manthan offshore scheme. Q1 PAT was also strong (₹81 cr). Watch: low base effect, vessel dry-dock days and charter renewals; CFO changed.

ROLEXRINGS.text: Forged bearing rings and auto components, about half exported. ==Q2 revenue +43% to ₹389 cr, PAT +68% to ₹74 cr== (about +32% excluding a one-time US duty refund). ==US sales more than doubled== as the US tariff disruption ended; ==auto-component exports +89%==. Monthly order book ₹120–125 cr and ==two new customer plants start supply in Q3/Q4==, so H2 should be stronger. Margins to return to 21–22% as sea freight eases. Watch: weak Europe bearing demand, fuel-gas costs.
sources: Multibagg – Rolex Rings FY28 margin outlook

LTFOODS.text: Basmati rice and food company (Daawat, Royal brands), strong in India and the US. ==Q2 revenue +17% to ₹3,234 cr; H1 revenue +22% to ₹6,414 cr==, H1 PAT ₹364 cr. ==India basmati market share up to 23.1%==, ==US basmati import share above 60%==, North America sales +49% in Q1. Acquired ==Leev== (new subsidiary). Guidance: FY27 revenue growth above 12%. Watch: profit growing slower than sales, loss-making ready-to-eat segment, US trade-duty case.
sources: Milling MEA – LT Foods Q2 FY27

TANFACIND.text: One of India's largest hydrofluoric acid (fluorine chemicals) makers, Cuddalore. ==Q2 revenue +39% to ₹234 cr – a record quarter==. ==FY27 growth guidance raised to 35–40% (from 30%)==. Big trigger: ==₹495 cr HFC-32 refrigerant gas plant (20,000 t/yr) to start in Q3 FY27==, with ==about two-thirds of capacity already contracted== with Japanese, MNC and Indian buyers; management sees ==~60% growth in FY28==. Watch: margin squeezed to 13% by sulphur costs; profit grew only ~11%.

SUPREMEPWR.text: Power and distribution transformer maker (up to 330 kV). ==H1 FY27 income +80% to ₹136 cr, PAT +45% to ₹13.7 cr==. ==Order book above ₹566 cr – about 3× FY26 revenue==; won ==11 orders worth ₹209 cr in H1==, including large 160 MVA/220 kV and 112.5 MVA/330 kV units, and entered Maharashtra. ==New Kannur plant ramping up== – lets it bid for bigger transformers. FY27 revenue target ₹275–300 cr. Watch: margins hit by raw-material inflation (70–75% of orders have price-variation clauses).
sources: Daily Guardian – Supreme Power H1 FY27

YATHARTH.text: Hospital chain in Delhi-NCR and UP. ==Q2 revenue +52% to ₹431 cr==, EBITDA +50%. ==New hospitals now 28% of revenue== (from 11%); Faridabad Sec-20 and Agra already EBITDA-positive. ==Occupancy up to 72% from 66%==, ==revenue per bed up 11% to ₹35,948==. ==250-bed Gurugram hospital due H1 FY28==; Advent partnership targets 7,000–8,000 beds. Watch: PAT grew only 17% (new-hospital ramp-up costs); Model Town not yet break-even.

ORIRAIL.text: Railway wagons, coach seats and berths maker. ==Q2 revenue ₹172.5 cr, PAT +43% to ₹15.3 cr==. ==Wagon output up 30% QoQ (~390 units)==. ==Order book ₹1,571 cr (2,000+ wagons)== – 3–4 quarters of visibility. Management guides ==H2 FY27 revenue 25–30% above H1==. Bidding for an RDSO smart-wagon tender (hopes for 200+ units); new bogie/gondola design going for approval. Wagon plant at only 50% use, so room to grow. Watch: Railway tender timing is uncertain.

MAYURUNIQ.text: Synthetic leather (PVC/PU) maker for car seats, footwear and furniture; supplies global auto OEMs in North America and Europe. ==Q1 FY27 standalone PAT +43% to ₹59 cr== with ==EBITDA margin ~30%==; consolidated revenue +25%. Growth comes from ==exports to global car makers==; management guides ==10–15% yearly revenue growth for three years== and says margins are sustainable. Watch: Q2 revenue grew only ~6%; PVC price swings, US freight and auto volumes.

SMT.text: Cardiac devices maker (stents, heart valves/TAVI, occluders), with 76% of sales from Europe and other exports. ==Q2 revenue +25% to ₹373 cr==, ==EBITDA +37% with record 17.6% margin==, PAT +27%. ==Structural heart (TAVI, occluders) growing ~40%==; India sales picked up to +15%. Guidance: ==margin to rise 150–200 bps a year, ~20% by FY29==. New launches pending: Sironity in India, Hydra Elevate approval. Watch: ~9% of growth came from currency; weak cash flow.

SOTL.text: Specialty oils maker – transformer oils, lubricants, white oils and esters. ==Q2 standalone PAT ₹216 cr vs ₹44 cr a year ago (~5×)==; ==petroleum products revenue +60% to ₹1,696 cr==. Q1 was a ==record quarter (PAT ₹292 cr)== on higher volumes and pricing. Demand helped by ==transformer oil for India's grid build-out== and its ester-based products. Watch: profit fell from Q1; jump may include inventory gains from base-oil price moves – may not repeat.

MATRIMONY.text: Online matchmaking (BharatMatrimony, Jeevansathi-rival). ==Q2 profit 2.7× to ₹20.7 cr==, revenue +18% to ₹135 cr, while ==costs rose only 2%== – strong operating leverage. ==Paid subscriptions up 27% to 3.02 lakh==. Buying a further 50% of ==Astro-Vision (astrology matchmaking)== for ₹8 cr. H1 profit +147%. Watch: billing fell 3.6% QoQ; wedding-services arm is shrinking.

NUVAMA.text: Wealth management, custody (asset services) and broking group. ==Q2 revenue +21% to ₹937 cr, operating profit +26% to ₹319 cr==, while ==costs grew only 16%==. ==Client assets up 25% to ₹5.5 lakh cr==. ==Asset Services revenue +53%== (custody/clearing for foreign and domestic funds); ==record net new money== in both Wealth and Private. ==SEBI approved its Numa SIF platform== – a new product line. Watch: capital-markets business depends on market mood; one-time ₹16 cr fund-closing charge.

SUDEEPPHRM.text: Maker of mineral-based ingredients (iron, calcium, zinc salts) for pharma, food and infant nutrition. ==Q2 record revenue ₹197 cr (+21%), EBITDA +32% with 37% margin==. ==Pharma-food-nutrition segment +57%== (72% of sales). New products (glycinates, gluconates, citrates) in the pipeline. Big new leg: ==Dahej battery-grade iron phosphate plant (25,000 t) for EV/storage batteries, from April 2027==. Watch: PAT grew only 11%; fortified-rice programme paused.

SAMBHV.text: Steel pipes and tubes maker (ERW, GI, hollow sections) with its own backward-integrated steel. ==Q2 revenue +44% to ₹836 cr, PAT doubled (+99%) to ₹61 cr==; ==value-added product sales 1.13 lakh t== (record volumes). H1 profit +82%. New growth leg: ==₹148 cr stainless steel seamless pipe plant in Chhattisgarh (14,400 t/yr) by March 2028==; more capacity commissioning in Q4 FY27. Watch: steel price swings, ~₹100 cr new debt, project timing.
sources: Free Press Journal – Sambhv Q2 FY27
Free Press Journal – Sambhv value-added volumes

PDSL.text: Global apparel sourcing and design company supplying big Western fashion brands. ==Record Q2 revenue ₹4,432 cr==; ==H1 revenue +23%, EBITDA +62%, PAT +44%==; margin up 77 bps. ==North America sales +44%== in H1 as brands shift sourcing; adding new customers and categories. ==Net cash ₹154 cr== and negative working capital. Interim dividend up 33%. Watch: thin margins (~1.6% PAT), newer ventures still turning profitable.

PANAMAPET.text: Specialty petroleum products maker – transformer oils, white oils, ink oils, lubricants – with export plants. ==Q2 revenue +123% to ₹1,722 cr, PAT 4.6× to ₹243 cr== (net margin 14% vs 7%); Q1 profit was also ₹309 cr. Demand supported by ==transformer oil for India's power grid== and higher product prices. Watch: profit swings sharply quarter to quarter (₹46–309 cr) – much of the jump likely comes from base-oil price moves and may not repeat.

MPSLTD.text: Content, platforms and e-learning services for global publishers and corporates. ==Q2 revenue +15% to ₹224 cr, EBITDA +27% with record 34.3% margin== (above 34% for two quarters). ==Core profit before tax +23%==. ==Billed clients up 90% to 933== – less dependence on a few clients. ==Debt-free== after repaying the Unbound Medicine acquisition loan; ₹163 cr cash. Corporate learning EBITDA nearly doubled. Watch: reported PAT -6% due to a one-time gain last year; revenue flat QoQ.

PRIMECAB.text: Power cable maker moving from LT to medium-voltage (MV, up to 33 kV) cables. ==H1 FY27 revenue +117% to ₹196 cr== (normalised +94%), ==PAT +73% to ₹9.5 cr==. ==Order book ₹294 cr==; private-sector sales more than tripled. ==New MV cable line at Giloth starts 21 Nov 2026 (up to ₹150 cr yearly sales)==, another plant in April 2027. FY27 target ₹370 cr revenue. Watch: commissioning already slipped once; thin ~5% margins; copper/aluminium prices.
